title: AWS Certified AI Practitioner
source: AWS AIF-C01 exam guide domains + in-scope services (Context syllabi)

domains.name: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions
Fundamentals of AI and ML
domains.subtitle: Domain 1 · 20% — concepts, use cases, ML lifecycle

services.name: Amazon SageMaker AI
services.desc: Managed platform to build, train, tune, and deploy ML models end-to-end.
examTopics: Stages of the AI/ML lifecycle: data prep → train → evaluate → deploy → monitor
Managed APIs vs self-hosted model serving tradeoffs
When custom ML is better than a foundation model (explainability, regulation, cost)
JumpStart for pre-trained models (also covered under GenAI)
services.tip: Map each lifecycle stage to an AWS capability — SageMaker is the backbone for custom ML.

services.name: Amazon Transcribe
services.desc: Speech-to-text service for converting audio into text.

services.name: Amazon Translate
services.desc: Neural machine translation between supported languages.
examTopics: When managed AI services beat custom models

services.name: Amazon Comprehend
services.desc: NLP for sentiment, entities, key phrases, PII detection, and classification.

services.name: Amazon Lex
services.desc: Conversational bots with ASR and NLU for chat/voice interfaces.
examTopics: Intent and slot concepts at a high level

services.name: Amazon Polly
services.desc: Text-to-speech synthesis for natural-sounding audio.

services.name: Amazon Quick
services.desc: Business intelligence and analytics experiences referenced for AI pipelines and insights.

services.name: Amazon Rekognition
services.desc: Computer vision for images and video (objects, faces, text, unsafe content).
examTopics: CV use cases vs building custom vision models

callouts.title: Core vocabulary to lock in
items: AI vs ML vs deep learning vs GenAI vs agentic AI
Supervised / unsupervised / reinforcement learning
Labeled vs unlabeled; structured vs unstructured data
Batch, real-time, asynchronous, and serverless inference

callouts.title: Exam traps
items: Picking GenAI when a deterministic rule or classic ML model is enough
Ignoring cost/latency when choosing real-time vs batch inference
Assuming every problem needs a custom-trained model

cards.title: Task map (Domain 1)
cards.intro: Align study to official task statements.
items: 1.1 Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
1.2 Identify practical use cases for AI (and when not to use AI)
1.3 Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle and AWS touchpoints

domains.name: Fundamentals of GenAI
domains.subtitle: Domain 2 · 24% — GenAI concepts, limits, AWS GenAI stack

services.name: Amazon Bedrock
services.desc: Fully managed access to foundation models via APIs, with tooling for apps, agents, and knowledge bases.
examTopics: Token-based pricing implications for cost and latency
Bedrock as the primary GenAI application platform on AWS
services.tip: Know Bedrock vs SageMaker: Bedrock = consume/customize FMs; SageMaker = build/train/host broadly.

services.name: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
services.desc: Hub of pre-trained models and solutions you can deploy and fine-tune.
examTopics: Overlap with Bedrock model choice questions

services.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
services.desc: Agent runtime capabilities for tool use, identity, and orchestration patterns on Bedrock.

services.name: Strands Agents
services.desc: Agent framework referenced for building multi-agent GenAI applications on AWS.
examTopics: When agents add value vs single-prompt apps

services.name: Kiro
services.desc: AWS AI-assisted development tooling referenced in AI lifecycle and GenAI app contexts.
examTopics: Developer productivity use cases for GenAI
Where AI assists the ML/app lifecycle

rows.val: Consuming FMs via API, RAG, agents, Guardrails
Prompts, RAG, fine-tuning/custom models where offered
Training custom models, full MLOps control
Higher — you own more of the pipeline

callouts.title: GenAI limitations to remember
items: Hallucinations, nondeterminism, weak interpretability
IP / trust / accuracy risks for business use
Token cost scales with context length and output

callouts.title: Must-know GenAI vocabulary
items: Tokens, embeddings, vectors, chunking, transformers/LLMs
Foundation models, multimodal, diffusion models
Prompt engineering and context engineering
MCP (Model Context Protocol) for connecting agents to tools

cards.title: Task map (Domain 2)
items: 2.1 Explain basic GenAI concepts
2.2 Capabilities and limitations for business problems
2.3 AWS infrastructure and technologies for GenAI apps

services.name: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
services.desc: Managed RAG: connect enterprise data to FMs with retrieval and grounding.
examTopics: RAG vs fine-tuning vs in-context learning vs distillation
services.tip: If the question emphasizes private/company data without full retraining → RAG.

services.name: Amazon OpenSearch Service
services.desc: Search and analytics engine commonly used as a vector store for embeddings.

services.name: Amazon Aurora
services.desc: Managed relational database; pgvector-style patterns for embeddings storage.

services.name: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
services.desc: Managed PostgreSQL suitable for vector/embedding workloads in RAG designs.

services.name: Amazon Neptune
services.desc: Graph database option for connected knowledge and some embedding/graph hybrid patterns.
examTopics: Graph relationships vs pure vector similarity

services.name: Prompt engineering patterns
services.desc: Techniques to steer FM behavior without changing model weights.

rows.val: Style/domain behavior must stick without huge context
Few examples fit in the prompt

callouts.title: Evaluation themes
items: Human eval, benchmark metrics, business KPIs (ROI, conversion, accuracy)
Latency, cost, and quality tradeoffs together
Detect hallucinations; validate grounded outputs

cards.title: Task map (Domain 3)
items: 3.1 Design considerations for FM applications
3.2 Effective prompt engineering
3.3 Training and fine-tuning process
3.4 Methods to evaluate FM performance

services.name: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
services.desc: Controls to filter harmful content, constrain topics, and apply safety policies to FM apps.
examTopics: Bias, fairness, inclusivity, robustness, safety, veracity
Legal risks: IP claims, biased outputs, customer trust, hallucinations
services.tip: Responsible AI questions often pair Guardrails with governance narratives.

callouts.title: Responsible AI checklist
items: Dataset diversity, balance, and curated sources
Bias vs variance effects (overfit/underfit, demographic harm)
Transparency and explainability expectations
Environmental / sustainability considerations in model choice

cards.title: Task map (Domain 4)
items: 4.1 Explain development of responsible AI systems
4.2 Recognize importance of transparent and explainable models

domains.name: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI
domains.subtitle: Domain 5 · 14% — secure AI systems and compliance
domains.quizTopic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

services.name: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
services.desc: Identities, roles, and policies controlling access to AI services and data.
examTopics: Least privilege for model invoke and data access

services.name: Amazon Macie
services.desc: Discovers and protects sensitive data (e.g., PII) in S3 — relevant to AI training data governance.

services.name: AWS PrivateLink
services.desc: Private connectivity to AWS services without traversing the public internet.
examTopics: Private access paths for AI APIs and data planes

services.name: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards
services.desc: Document model details, intended use, and evaluation for governance and lineage.

services.name: Encryption & shared responsibility
services.desc: Protect data at rest and in transit; understand AWS vs customer responsibilities for AI workloads.
examTopics: Prompt injection and data leakage risks

callouts.title: Security traps
items: Training on sensitive data without classification/controls
Exposing model endpoints publicly without authz
Ignoring prompt injection / tool-abuse in agents

cards.title: Task map (Domain 5)
items: 5.1 Methods to secure AI systems
5.2 Governance and compliance regulations for AI systems

strategy.title: Lock the vocabulary first
items: Write one-line definitions for AI, ML, DL, GenAI, FM, LLM, RAG, fine-tuning, embeddings, tokens, agents.
For each term, note one AWS service that maps to it.
Drill differences: RAG vs fine-tune vs prompt-only.

strategy.title: Scenario technique
items: Identify: custom ML vs FM vs managed AI API.
Check constraints: latency, cost, private data, explainability, safety.
Prefer simplest compliant option (managed API → Bedrock/RAG → fine-tune/custom).

strategy.title: High-frequency traps
items: Hallucinations → grounding/RAG/Guardrails, not “just raise temperature”.
Private enterprise knowledge → Knowledge Bases / vector store, not only longer prompts.
Responsible AI is scored — do not skip Domains 4–5.

strategy.title: High-ROI study order
items: Domain 3 (28%) applications of FMs
Domain 2 (24%) GenAI fundamentals + Bedrock
Domain 1 (20%) AI/ML basics + managed AI services
Domains 4–5 (14% each) responsible AI + security

checklist.text: Define AI, ML, DL, GenAI, agentic AI and give an example of each
Contrast supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning
Explain batch vs real-time vs asynchronous vs serverless inference
Map ML lifecycle stages to SageMaker AI capabilities
Know when NOT to use AI/ML (determinism, cost-benefit)
Define tokens, embeddings, vectors, chunking, transformers
Describe FM lifecycle from selection through feedback
Explain token-based pricing impact on cost/latency
List GenAI limitations: hallucination, nondeterminism, interpretability
Position Amazon Bedrock vs SageMaker JumpStart
Choose FM by modality, latency, cost, context length, customization
Explain temperature and max token effects on outputs
Describe RAG and Bedrock Knowledge Bases business use
Name embeddings storage options: OpenSearch, Aurora, RDS, Neptune
Compare RAG, fine-tuning, in-context learning, distillation costs
Apply zero-shot / few-shot / structured prompt patterns
Describe agent tool-use and multi-agent patterns at a high level
List FM evaluation approaches (human, metrics, business KPIs)
Name responsible AI dimensions and Bedrock Guardrails role
Identify legal/IP and trust risks of GenAI deployments
Explain bias/variance and dataset diversity impacts
Apply IAM least privilege to model invoke and data access
Describe encryption, PrivateLink, and Macie in AI data paths
Use Model Cards / lineage for governance documentation
Mitigate prompt injection, leakage, and missing audit trails

phases.title: GenAI core + FM apps
phases.focus: Domain 2–3: Bedrock, tokens/embeddings, RAG vs fine-tune, prompts, evaluation

phases.title: AI/ML fundamentals
phases.focus: Domain 1: vocabulary, use cases, lifecycle, managed AI services (Transcribe, Comprehend, Lex, etc.)

phases.title: Responsible AI + security
phases.focus: Domains 4–5: Guardrails, fairness, IAM, encryption, Model Cards, prompt injection

phases.title: Review & weak spots
phases.focus: Revisit Domain 3 scenarios, checklist mastery, Skill Builder practice if available
